question: What Na content did ion chromatography find in the original sawdust and in the original lignite used for fast co-pyrolysis?
trap: the 0.79 wt% Na of the loaded sawdust or the 2 wt% NaCl
rendered:
<document title="Effects of sodium on nitrogen evolution characteristics during the fast co-pyrolysis of coal and biomass">

=== page 1 ===
- Acid-washed and Na-loaded samples, including individual SD/LC and blended samples (blending ratios of 5% and 15%), were pyrolyzed in a vertical fixed-bed reactor at 500 °C and 800 °C. The results demonstrate that Na promotes the release of NH3 and HCN during the pyrolysis of SD at 500 °C but inhibits it at 800 °C, whereas for LC and all blended samples, Na suppresses the release of both species at 500 °C and 800 °C.

=== page 2 ===
- The results show that at low temperatures of 500 °C, labile biomass N-A decomposes into NH3, while coal N-5 and N-6 remain relatively stable. At 800 °C, heterocyclic nitrogen undergoes ring-opening to form HCN, while coal preferentially retains nitrogen as N-Q. Crucially, Na addition alters these pathways, promoting the apparent NH3 and HCN release from biomass at 500 °C while inhibiting heterocyclic ring-opening and N-Q hydrogenation at 800 °C.

=== page 2 ===
- The sodium (Na) content in the raw materials was quantied using ion chromatography (IC, DIONEX AQ-1100), yielding 0.27% for SD-original and 2.75% for LC-original.

The Na content in the original sawdust (SD) was 0.27%, and in the original lignite (LC) was 2.75%.
